body.statement: Establish one of two separator-boundary results. On the positive branch, using the factorized handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{sep}}\), output every \(F_{\ell,A}\) and every dense \(Q_{\ell}\) exactly from a width-\(w\) decomposition in \(Ln^2 2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)\) bit operations. Combined with the standard finite-SDP proposition, this branch returns \(q^{\star}\), \(\nu^{\star}\), and a primal--dual zero-gap certificate in total time \(Ln^2 2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)+(\Lambda Ln)^{2^{O(L+n^2)}}\). On the negative branch, establish \(\#\mathrm{W[1]}\)-hardness or \(\mathrm{W[1]}\)-hardness parameterized by \(w\) for one required one- or two-marked coefficient under positive weights bounded by \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\). Either branch settles the separator boundary for the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count oracle. The positive-branch certificate concerns this restricted oracle and is neither an algorithm for nor a consequence of the unrestricted design-and-estimator maximal-independent-set functional.
body.justification: This positive-versus-hard theorem-level target is the tier-bearing contribution: it resolves whether separator joins admit exact fixed-parameter integration and converts the positive resolution into an auditable minimax WRI design.
body.gap: Kangas, Koivisto, and Salonen provide only an XP order-counting analogue. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje study an implicit unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax functional in Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, but do not compute the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count oracle or provide its fixed-parameter risk certificate.
body.consumer: A positive branch supplies an explicit low-treewidth runtime and certified mixture for the rural-China insurance-information follow-up; a negative branch gives a parameterized reason to use the arbitrary-graph Monte Carlo certificate.
